text:
infra-monitor-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node gpu-prod-12 reporting localSSD usage 98% (eviction pressure). 12 pods in node-slice-3 showing Terminated/OOMKILL or Evicted. Auto-escalating to #incidents at priority P1.

maria_g: seeing repeated eviction events for /var/lib/modelcache, logs flooded. modelcache dir at 92GB, node has 100GB localSSD. Suspect runaway cache warm.

kevin_w: copying logs — getting tons of `ENOSPC` in runtime: `2026-03-15T14:02:11Z runtime: failed to write cache chunk: ENOSPC`

platform-sre: confirmed: kubelet eviction triggered for imagefs.available< node.fs.available threshold. Pods with local model cache got evicted first.

maria_g: impacted service: /v1/generate on dedicated pool east-us-2. Latency and 503s reported by customer telemetry.

tanvi_r: paging oncall and starting mitigation: can we cordon gpu-prod-12 and drain non-critical pods? @oncall-rotation can you take action?

oncall-rotation: I'm on it, cordoning node now: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-prod-12
kubectl drain gpu-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

kevin_w: be careful, deleting local-data will clear model caches and cause cold starts. prefer to evict only cache-heavy pods and restart runtime with reduced cache size.

platform-sre: good call. I'll patch the runtime config for the node pool to set MODEL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=20GB via a rolling update on the daemonset. That should free space gradually without killing all pods.

maria_g: patch command snippet: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/runtime-daemon MODEL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=21474836480
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime-daemon -n infra
```

oncall-rotation: applying now. Rolling restart started for runtime-daemon across node-slice-3.

customer-ops: FYI customers in orgs A and C are seeing errors; I've opened a ticket and linked to this thread. Flagging potential SLA impact.

tanvi_r: while the daemonset rolls, I'm going to delete a few of the largest modelcache dirs on the affected node to free immediate space. Listing top dirs: 
```
sudo du -sh /var/lib/modelcache/* | sort -h | tail -n 10
```

kevin_w: please snapshot first for analysis: `tar -czf /tmp/modelcache-snap-$(date +%s).tgz /var/lib/modelcache/huge-model` then rm -rf. We need one copy for debugging.

maria_g: did that for two largest models. Freed ~40GB. kubelet eviction events dropped. Some pods restarted cleanly.

infra-monitor-bot: Node gpu-prod-12 localSSD usage dropped to 64%, eviction pressure reduced.

platform-sre: runtime rollout reached 60% on the pool — new env var limits cache to 20GB, subsequent cache writes are being throttled.

maria_g: still seeing CUDA allocation errors in a handful of containers after restart: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`. Those look secondary — they happen when runtime restarts and tries to reload full model into GPU. We'll backoff GPU loads temporarily.

tanvi_r: adding temporary admission controller patch to set MAX_GPU_LOAD_CONCURRENCY=1 for the dedicated namespace to avoid simultaneous full-model loads. Applying now.

oncall-rotation: done. New admission policy applied: no more than 1 concurrent model load job per node for that namespace.

kevin_w: observed one customer-facing route still returning 503 intermittently. Handoff to next oncall in 30m. @platform-sre please keep monitoring for flapping; set an auto-fallback to smaller quantized model if node capacity drops below threshold.

platform-sre: setting routing policy: fallback to model-v2-quantized when region capacity < 40%. Patching route.

customer-ops: reached out to affected customers with a status note: "We detected local disk pressure causing model cache evictions. We have freed space and implemented temporary limits; you may see reduced throughput while caches rebuild. Root cause investigation ongoing."

maria_g: creating incident ticket and collecting logs: `kubectl -n infra logs daemonset/runtime-daemon --since=2h` and `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200`

kevin_w: capture kubelet eviction log snippet for postmortem: 
```
Mar 15 14:01:22 gpu-prod-12 kubelet: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
Mar 15 14:01:22 gpu-prod-12 kubelet: Evicting pod infra/runtime-pod-54 due to imagefs.available
```

infra-monitor-bot: P1 incident created: INC-2026-341. Current status: mitigated (node cordoned + cache limit + admission throttle + fallback). Root cause: aggressive model cache fill on localSSD combined with insufficient eviction protection.

tanvi_r: next steps: collect full modelcache sizes per node, add K8s localssd alert at 85% with automated scale/burst policy, and record runbook changes to avoid rm -rf manual steps. Assigning followups to @maria_g and @platform-sre.

oncall-rotation: handing off to next oncall in 25m. I'll leave monitoring playbook and keep watch for 1hr after handoff.

maria_g: will own RCA and remediation tickets. Adding notes to customer ticket once RCA draft ready.

kevin_w: log of actions appended to incident ticket. Good work everyone. :thumbsup:
